description: CNY per USD derived as (CNY per EUR)/(USD per EUR) from Eurostat annual averages
basis: Customs implied rates vary 0.3-2.6% across codes within a month, so no single customs rate exists

description: Foreign front-end CMP declared under 84862090 rather than 84861040
basis: Hwatsing share on an 84861040-only basis is 45-47% (2024-25, upper bound) vs independent estimates of 30-45%; the gap implies $0-260m a year
source: China Customs Data Exploration (vault Tier 3), CMP classification test 2026-09-23

description: Vendor revenue without a China/overseas split is treated as China supply (upper bound)
basis: CEPEA front-end exports were 8-9% of front-end revenue in 2024-25; Yitang (Mattson) and ACM carry larger overseas shares and are flagged

description: Calendar-year revenue (acceptance basis) is compared with calendar-year imports (declaration basis) without a lag
basis: Acceptance usually lags shipment by months; not modelled in the first pass

description: Share of 84864039 (other lifting/handling of boules, wafers, devices, ICs and flat panels) that is fab automation bought by wafer fabs
basis: The code mixes flat-panel handling (declaration example: LCD glass panel loader) with wafer-transfer robots imported as tool modules (example: Lam-branded wafer-handling arm), which domestic tool revenue already contains. In 2025 Korean origin rose from 23% to 43% and Sichuan consignees from 7% to 31% of value, a pattern consistent with display-line handling (hypothesis, unverified). Base excludes the code; high counts half as fab automation
source: Atlas statistics/china_customs (848640, pulled 2026-09-28); transcustoms.cn 8486403900 declaration examples

description: Share of 84862090 value that is wet cleaning equipment (single-wafer, batch, spin-rinse-dry)
basis: Wet cleaners are 31 of 255 non-part declaration examples under 8486209000 (16% of those not PCB/solar misdeclarations), mainly SCREEN/DNS and Semitool models. Counts are not value: cleaners are high-value tools ($3-8m), and the code average rose to $1.5m/item in 2025 as cheap items fell away. No vendor-side value anchor yet (SCREEN/TEL China cleaning sales would tighten it)
source: Declaration examples (docs/customs_code_evidence.md, Tier 4); Atlas statistics/china_customs unit values

description: Share of 84862090 value that is back-end equipment (dicing saws, back-grinders, die bonders)
basis: Dicing saws, grinders and die bonders are 46 of about 190 semiconductor declaration examples under 8486209000. By value they are smaller: die bonders average about $0.26m/item under 84864029 against $1.5m/item for 84862090 in 2025. The US classifies dicing saws under 8486.20, not assembly (N361145), so they legitimately sit here. No vendor-side anchor yet (DISCO China sales would tighten it)
source: Declaration examples (docs/customs_code_evidence.md, Tier 4); Atlas statistics/china_customs unit values

description: NAURA product lines reported only as floors ("over CNY X bn") grow at least in line with its electronic process equipment segment: base = max(floor, prior-year base x segment growth); low = the floor; high = base +30% (tier C default), never above the floor plus the whole unallocated segment residual
basis: Estimation standards section 5: a floor may carry a base above it only with evidence. The segment total is reported exactly each year and constrains the lines; growth-carried anchors are the evidence. The high case is an absolute cap, not a likely value

description: Share of Kingsemi FY2025 revenue consolidated into NAURA (control from 2025-06-23)
basis: About 52% of the year after the control date, assuming even revenue. Removed both from NAURA's residual cap and (from 7 Oct 2026) from the 2025 process-equipment growth factor that carries NAURA's floor-only lines, so Kingsemi is not counted twice or used to inflate NAURA's own lines
